title: Replaying 'Kingdom Hearts': A Fan Misses the Final Fantasy Friends
summary:
The video game website Kotaku is replaying the whole 'Kingdom Hearts' series over a year in a kind of book club called Guiding Key. The next main game, 'Kingdom Hearts IV,' is expected in about a year. In the latest entry, the writer looks back at how the first game brought in characters from the 'Final Fantasy' series.

'Kingdom Hearts' is a crossover that mixes Disney characters like Donald Duck and Goofy with heroes from 'Final Fantasy,' a long-running role-playing game series. The main hero is a boy named Sora.

The writer explains that when they first played as a kid, they did not even know some characters came from 'Final Fantasy.' Now, after playing many 'Final Fantasy' games, they notice much more.

On Sora's home, Destiny Islands, his friends include Tidus and Wakka from 'Final Fantasy X' and Selphie from 'Final Fantasy VIII.' They are younger than in their own games and use playground versions of their weapons. Tidus swings a wooden practice sword, and Selphie uses a jump rope.

In Traverse Town, a safe place for people whose worlds are disappearing, Sora meets more familiar faces, including Leon, Yuffie and Aerith. The writer says these characters feel much closer to their original versions. They also enjoy the funny first meeting between Sora, Donald and Goofy, and the town's music.

The writer's main point is that 'Final Fantasy' characters have played a smaller and smaller part in later games. 'Kingdom Hearts III' did not include any until extra content was added. The writer wonders whether newer 'Final Fantasy' heroes might appear in 'Kingdom Hearts IV.'
why_it_matters: The column shows how fans think about crossovers and what they hope to see in the next game, which is expected in about a year.
